headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: open-webui can ingest files, MCP, and external APIs while dagster is a non-runnable orchestrator with no direct I/O, making the pair unsafe by default for sensitive workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can consume files, MCP, plugins, and OpenAPI tool servers, so attacker-controlled content can reach its instruction layer; dagster has no direct I/O surfaces or runtime to sanitize anything. The interaction is plausible in default web-app usage, but dagster itself does not create the bridge, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF open-webui is connected to an MCP or OpenAPI tool that returns untrusted content, prompt injection is possible.
IF dagster outputs are copied into open-webui prompts or files, those outputs can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Disable MCP/OpenAPI tools for untrusted sources.
Add a fixed instruction delimiter before any imported content.
Route dagster outputs through a human review step before ingestion.
Use separate workspaces for generated artifacts and prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content filtering at the web-ui boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches files, mounted volumes, persistent memory, API keys, and broad external services by default; dagster is a data-engineering orchestrator that may produce artifacts but has no built-in isolation here. If sensitive data enters open-webui, its broad egress and integrations can exfiltrate it, while dagster provides no compensating control in the profile.
conditions: IF sensitive files are mounted into open-webui, they can be exposed to its inference and tool stack.
IF open-webui is configured with external APIs or search tools, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Remove sensitive mounts from open-webui.
Rotate any API keys exposed to the web UI.
Disable external search and API tools for sensitive sessions.
Keep dagster artifacts in a separate non-mounted directory.
requires-engineering: enforce per-workspace access controls and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dagster is non-runnable and has no write or network capabilities in the profile, while open-webui supports persistent shared sessions, local files, mounted volumes, and broad networked tools. There is no direct same-dir write conflict shown, but open-webui can still contend over shared artifacts or session state if the operator co-locates them.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted volume, open-webui can overwrite or mutate artifacts dagster expects to be stable.
IF open-webui shares session-backed state across instances, concurrent edits can race on shared resources.
mitigations: Use separate directories for dagster outputs and open-webui uploads.
Avoid sharing a mounted volume between the two agents.
Turn off multi-instance shared sessions for sensitive work.
Snapshot artifacts before handing them to open-webui.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable workspace.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui is designed to render and act on model outputs via tools, plugins, and function calling, so if dagster-produced artifacts are fed into it, they can be treated as authoritative without verification. Dagster does not provide a verification layer in the profile, making downstream mistakes likely and potentially action-bearing.
conditions: IF dagster-generated text is pasted or imported into open-webui, open-webui may present it as trusted context.
IF open-webui is connected to action-capable tools, incorrect dagster outputs can trigger downstream actions.
mitigations: Require human verification before any tool action.
Mark dagster outputs as untrusted in the UI.
Disable action-capable plugins for imported content.
Use a checksum or schema check on dagster artifacts before ingestion.
requires-engineering: add an explicit verification gate between generation and action.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, documents, notes, calendar events, and persistent memory, and can send data to third-party APIs; dagster is a data-engineering system that may route regulated data into those flows. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so this is a policy-mismatch risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is loaded into open-webui, its external API integrations may violate local handling policy.
IF dagster pipelines feed data into open-webui without retention controls, retention and deletion obligations can diverge.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into open-webui.
Disable persistent memory for sensitive tenants.
Review retention settings before importing documents.
Keep API keys out of shared chat contexts.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement per workspace.
